intent_evidence.source: Dockerfiles/server-mysql/README.md L87 (near-identical wording also at Dockerfiles/web-apache-mysql/README.md L93, substituting "web-interface" for "server")
intent_evidence.quote: These variables are used by Zabbix server to connect to Zabbix database. With the `_FILE` variables you can instead provide the path to a file which contains the user / the password instead. Without Docker Swarm or Kubernetes you also have to map the files.

deploy_blocker.summary: D1-D4 run normally against this manifest (static analysis, security scan, requirement checks need no live cluster). D5/D6 (real deployment, fault injection) cannot complete on this test cluster: a kubelet/containerd bug in this kind cluster's k8s v1.37.0 makes any pod that mounts the SAME Secret twice (as two volumes with different `items` key-remappings) fail container creation permanently with "error mounting ... to rootfs at /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount ... read-only file system". kubernetes.yaml legitimately does this for db-secret (split into mysql-credentials/mysql-admin-credentials), which is a normal, valid Kubernetes pattern -- not a defect in the manifest.
deploy_blocker.isolated_with: Standalone repro pods on 2026-10-21: a Pod mounting the same Secret twice this way fails deterministically and reproducibly across fresh namespaces, a node restart, and different worker nodes; a Pod with two DIFFERENT secrets (no remapping) and a Pod with the real PVC alone both succeed, isolating the duplicate-secret-volume pattern as the trigger rather than disk/memory pressure, node-specific state, or the mysql/zabbix-web images themselves.
deploy_blocker.decision: Kept in the dataset for D1-D4; D5/D6 results for this project are recorded as not-applicable with this note, documented in the paper's Threats to Validity rather than treated as a manifest or dataset defect.
